concerns.text: The Piecewise Linear Regression (PLR) is fit using only four library‑size points (10, 30, 50, 100). With so few observations, estimating a breakpoint is under‑determined and yields low statistical power, threatening the validity of the claimed “tipping point” (SC‑004).

The PLR model ignores the semantic‑overlap factor, yet overlap levels (low/medium/high) are known to affect retrieval noise. Treating library size as the sole predictor risks confounding, because overlap‑induced redundancy may drive changes in success rate rather than size alone.

Retrieval Diversity is defined as the “inverse of the variance of the cosine similarities of the top‑k retrieved skills against the task’s ground‑truth set.” This construct is ambiguous: variance can be zero, leading to infinite values, and it mixes similarity to ground truth with diversity among retrieved items, making it unclear what aspect of diversity is being measured.
